titulo: Pretérito imperfecto: Ser, ir, ver and the uses of the imperfecto

aula.objetivo: Form the pretérito imperfecto of -ar, -er and -ir verbs and the three irregulars (ser, ir, ver), and use it for past habits, descriptions, age, time, and weather, while avoiding three false friends: «exquisito», «embarazada», and «raro».

sessao.titulo: Ser, ir, ver and the uses of the imperfecto

blocos.titulo: Ser, ir, ver, and when to use the imperfecto
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: only three verbs are irregular in the imperfecto: «ser», «ir», and «ver». STEP 2: «ser» becomes era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran. «Ir» becomes iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban. «Ver» becomes veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían. STEP 3: the accent shows up in «éramos» and «íbamos»; in «veía» it marks the strong «i». STEP 4: the first use is a past habit: «Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo» (every summer we'd go to the village). Sentences like this talk about what used to repeat. STEP 5: the second use is describing people and things in the past: «Mi abuela era alta y llevaba gafas» (my grandmother was tall and wore glasses). STEP 6: the third use is age, time, and weather: «Tenía diez años», «Eran las ocho», «Hacía frío», «Llovía». STEP 7: the fourth use is setting the scene or a state: «La casa estaba en una colina», «Mi tío estaba cansado». STEP 8: in all these cases the fact has no clear beginning or end. For a single, closed-off fact (ayer, el lunes), go back to the indefinido. Lesson 22 covers that choice. STEP 9: in Latin America, «de chico, de chica» is common in place of «de niño, de niña», and «de grande» in place of «de mayor».
blocos.comparacao: English «was/were» and «used to go» map closely onto «era» and «iba» for description and habit, so that part feels familiar. What's new is that Spanish treats age, time, and weather in the past (tenía diez años, eran las ocho, hacía frío) as part of this same imperfecto system — a single grammatical category — where English just uses its ordinary past tense for all of these with no special marking at all («I was ten», «it was eight o'clock», «it was cold»), so there's no verb-shape cue in English to flag this as a distinct use.

exemplos.ru: Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo de mi madre.
exemplos.pt: Every summer we used to go to my mother's hometown.

exemplos.ru: Mi abuelo era alto y siempre llevaba sombrero.
exemplos.pt: My grandfather was tall and always wore a hat.

exemplos.ru: Eran las nueve y hacía mucho calor.
exemplos.pt: It was nine o'clock and it was very hot.

exemplos.ru: Yo tenía siete años y veía la tele con mi hermano.
exemplos.pt: I was seven and I used to watch TV with my brother.

erros.motivo: Age at a point in the past is a description: use the imperfecto «tenía».

erros.errado: [misto] Eran las nueve y hizo calor.
erros.certo: [misto] Eran las nueve y hacía calor.
erros.motivo: Weather as the backdrop of a scene goes in the imperfecto: «hacía».

blocos.enunciado: Describe out loud, in at least eight sentences, the place where you used to spend your vacations, or a relative's house, as a child: what it was like, who was there, what you used to do. Use «era», «tenía», «hacía», «íbamos», and «veía».
Conjugate «hablar» and «vivir» in the imperfecto. Say one sentence with «antes» and another with «de pequeño».
